**Problem:**
Sometimes album artwork has unexpected dimensions or aspect ratios, causing it to render oversized and break the Listen page layout. The artwork can occupy a huge area in the top-left corner, leaving excessive empty space and disrupting the hero section.

**Requirements:**

1. Inspect the existing Listen tab implementation and identify the artwork container and relevant CSS.
2. Make the hero section dimensions consistent, regardless of the artwork's intrinsic dimensions.
3. NEVER stretch or distort artwork. Always preserve its original aspect ratio.
4. Display the original artwork prominently using `object-fit: contain`.
5. Use an enlarged, cropped, blurred copy of the same artwork as the background to fill the hero section naturally. Apply a dark overlay/gradient so text remains readable.
6. Ensure the background image is clipped to its container and cannot overflow into other page sections.
7. Handle missing, invalid, or failed artwork gracefully using Puffin's existing fallback artwork if available.
8. Ensure the layout remains responsive on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

**Important constraints:**
- Only modify the Listen tab's artwork presentation and the CSS/markup directly required for it.
- Do not change metadata retrieval, artwork selection, image URLs, playback functionality, or other pages.
- Preserve Puffin's existing visual design language, typography, spacing, and teal accents.
- Avoid unnecessary JavaScript or additional dependencies.

**Validation:**
Test with square, portrait, landscape, unusually large, and missing artwork. None should distort the image, overflow its container, or break the hero layout.

Keep the implementation clean and minimal. Do not redesign the entire Listen page.

    import { listMediaFiles, listPlaylists, listRecentlyPlayed } from "./library.js";
    
    export function initializeListen({ onPlay }) {
      const featured = document.querySelector("#listen-featured");
      const recent = document.querySelector("#listen-recent");
      const recentEmpty = document.querySelector("#listen-recent-empty");
      const library = document.querySelector("#listen-library");
      const empty = document.querySelector("#listen-empty");
      const search = document.querySelector("#listen-search");
      const playlistSelect = document.querySelector("#listen-playlist");
      let songs = [];
      let recentSongs = [];
      let playlists = [];
    
      const titleOf = (song) => song.title || song.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
      const artworkFor = (song, className) => {
        const img = document.createElement("img");
        img.className = className;
        img.src = song.artwork || "/favicon.svg";
        img.alt = "";
        img.loading = "lazy";
        img.addEventListener("error", () => { if (!img.src.endsWith("/favicon.svg")) img.src = "/favicon.svg"; }, { once: true });
        return img;
      };
      const makeRow = (song, compact = false) => {
        const card = document.createElement("article");
        card.className = compact ? "watch-video-card watch-video-card-compact" : "watch-video-card";
        card.setAttribute("role", "listitem");
        const button = document.createElement("button");
        button.type = "button";
        button.className = "watch-thumbnail-button listen-art-button";
        button.setAttribute("aria-label", `Play ${titleOf(song)}`);
        const art = artworkFor(song, "listen-artwork");
        const play = document.createElement("span");
        play.className = "watch-thumbnail-mark";
        play.textContent = "▶";
        button.append(art, play);
        button.addEventListener("click", () => onPlay(song));
        const title = document.createElement("button");
        title.type = "button";
        title.className = "watch-video-title-button";
        const heading = document.createElement("h3");
        heading.textContent = titleOf(song);
        title.append(heading);
        title.addEventListener("click", () => onPlay(song));
        const metadata = document.createElement("p");
        metadata.className = "watch-video-metadata";
        metadata.textContent = [song.artist, song.album].filter(Boolean).join(" · ") || "Puffin Library";
        card.append(button, title, metadata);
        return card;
      };
    
      function render() {
        recent.replaceChildren(...recentSongs.slice(0, 12).map((song) => makeRow(song, true)));
        recentEmpty.hidden = recentSongs.length > 0;
        const latest = recentSongs[0] || songs[0];
        featured.replaceChildren();
        if (latest) {
          const hero = document.createElement("article");
          hero.className = "watch-featured-card listen-featured-card";
          const art = artworkFor(latest, "watch-featured-art");
          const copy = document.createElement("div");
          copy.className = "watch-featured-copy";
          const eyebrow = document.createElement("p");
          eyebrow.className = "watch-eyebrow";
          eyebrow.textContent = recentSongs.length ? "PICK UP THE MUSIC" : "YOUR MUSIC LIBRARY";
          const heading = document.createElement("h2");
          heading.textContent = titleOf(latest);
          const byline = document.createElement("p");
          byline.className = "watch-featured-metadata";
          byline.textContent = [latest.artist, latest.album].filter(Boolean).join(" · ");
          const play = document.createElement("button");
          play.type = "button";
          play.className = "primary-button watch-featured-play";
          play.textContent = "Play";
          play.addEventListener("click", () => onPlay(latest));
          copy.append(eyebrow, heading, byline, play);
          hero.append(art, copy);
          featured.append(hero);
        }
        const query = search.value.toLocaleLowerCase().trim();
        const selected = playlists.find((item) => item.id === playlistSelect.value);
        const selectedIds = selected ? new Set(selected.mediaIds) : null;
        const filtered = songs.filter((song) => {
          if (selectedIds && !selectedIds.has(song.id)) return false;
          return !query || [titleOf(song), song.artist, song.album, song.genre].join(" ").toLocaleLowerCase().includes(query);
        });
        library.replaceChildren(...filtered.map((song) => makeRow(song)));
        empty.hidden = filtered.length > 0;
      }
    
      async function load() {
        const [records, playlistsNext, recentNext] = await Promise.all([listMediaFiles(), listPlaylists(), listRecentlyPlayed()]);
        songs = records.filter((record) => record.kind === "audio");
        playlists = playlistsNext.filter((playlist) => playlist.mediaIds.some((id) => songs.some((song) => song.id === id)));
        recentSongs = recentNext.filter((record) => record.kind === "audio");
        const oldValue = playlistSelect.value;
        playlistSelect.replaceChildren(new Option("All playlists", "all"));
        playlists.forEach((playlist) => playlistSelect.add(new Option(playlist.name, playlist.id)));
        playlistSelect.value = playlists.some((playlist) => playlist.id === oldValue) ? oldValue : "all";
        render();
      }
      search.addEventListener("input", render);
      playlistSelect.addEventListener("change", render);
      window.addEventListener("puffin:library-updated", load);
      window.addEventListener("puffin:metadata-updated", load);
      window.addEventListener("puffin:recently-played-updated", load);
      window.addEventListener("puffin:tab-changed", (event) => { if (event.detail === "listen") load(); });
      load();
    }

## User

Fix the Listen tab's hero artwork layout while preserving the existing two-column design.

**IMPORTANT: I LIKE THE CURRENT DESIGN DIRECTION. DO NOT REDESIGN IT.**

The intended layout is:
- Album artwork on the LEFT.
- Song title, artist, album, and Play button on the RIGHT.
- A dark, atmospheric background spanning the entire hero section.
- Rounded corners and the existing visual styling.

**Current problems:**
- The artwork is excessively large and appears vertically stretched.
- The right-hand content area is empty instead of displaying the song information.
- The artwork and content are not properly balanced within the hero section.

**Fixes:**

1. Preserve the two-column layout on desktop.
2. Give the artwork a consistent, bounded container with a square aspect ratio.
3. Display the original artwork using `object-fit: contain` so it NEVER stretches or distorts.
4. Vertically center the artwork within its container.
5. Place the song title, artist, album, and Play button in the RIGHT column, vertically centered and properly spaced.
6. Use the artwork as a subtle, blurred background across the hero section, with a dark overlay for readability.
7. Keep the hero section's height and proportions consistent across different artwork dimensions.
8. Ensure the artwork cannot overflow its container or force the hero section to expand.
9. On smaller screens, adapt the layout gracefully, stacking the artwork and song information if necessary.

**Visual direction:**
Think polished Apple Music / Sonos-style music player. Generous spacing, strong typography, restrained effects, and clear visual hierarchy.

**Strict constraints:**
- Do not change the overall two-column composition.
- Do not modify metadata retrieval, artwork selection, playback, or backend functionality.
- Do not modify unrelated pages or components.
- Avoid unnecessary JavaScript and dependencies.
- Reuse existing styles and components wherever possible.

Before implementing, inspect the current Listen page markup and CSS to identify why the artwork is being rendered incorrectly.

I found the player state is held in memory in `main.js`; the queue, current position, shuffle, repeat, and visualizer settings are lost on reload. I’m persisting that snapshot locally and restoring the track paused at its saved position when Puffin reopens, so browser autoplay restrictions don’t prevent recovery.

## User

## Puffin — Queue UX & Interaction Upgrade

Improve Puffin's existing playback queue to feel polished, fluid, and intuitive, taking inspiration from the queue interactions in Spotify and Apple Music.

**Important:** This is an enhancement of the existing queue, not a complete redesign. Preserve Puffin's current visual identity, typography, colors, spacing, and overall layout. Avoid unnecessary changes to unrelated pages or functionality.

### 1. Individual movable queue items

The current queue has an issue where songs appear to teleport between positions when reordered.

Replace this behavior with a more sophisticated drag-and-drop interaction:

- Each queue item should behave like an independent movable card/box.
- When dragging a song, that specific item should visually lift from the list, with a subtle scale, shadow, and elevation effect.
- As the dragged item moves over other songs, neighboring items should smoothly animate out of the way.
- The dragged item should follow the pointer or touch position naturally.
- When released, it should smoothly settle into its new position.
- Avoid instantaneous DOM repositioning or visual teleportation.
- Use smooth, carefully tuned animations with appropriate easing.
- Support both mouse and touchscreen interactions.
- Provide clear visual feedback for the currently dragged item and its intended drop position.

The result should feel comparable in quality to Spotify or Apple Music's queue reordering.

### 2. Queue management actions

Build on the existing queue functionality rather than duplicating it.

Add support for:
- **Play Next:** Insert a selected track immediately after the currently playing track.
- **Add to Queue:** Append a selected track to the end of the queue.
- **Remove from Queue:** Remove an individual queued track.
- **Clear Queue:** Clear upcoming tracks with an appropriate confirmation if necessary.
- Preserve existing drag-and-drop reordering.

Expose these actions through appropriate track context menus or existing UI controls. Keep the interface uncluttered.

### 3. Queue persistence

Make sure queue changes are reflected in the existing playback-session persistence system.

Specifically:
- Persist the updated queue after every reorder.
- Persist changes after Play Next, Add to Queue, Remove, and Clear Queue.
- Preserve the current track and playback position when the upcoming queue changes.
- Ensure the restored queue maintains its exact order after reopening Puffin.
- Avoid accidentally restoring tracks that the user deliberately removed.

### 4. Animation and performance requirements

- Animations should feel fluid, not exaggerated.
- Avoid unnecessary layout recalculations or expensive animation techniques.
- Prefer transform and opacity animations where appropriate.
- Avoid animating the entire queue unnecessarily.
- Prevent accidental playback when the user intended to drag a track.
- Ensure the queue remains responsive with large libraries and long queues.
- Respect reduced-motion accessibility preferences.

### 5. Implementation constraints

- First inspect the existing queue implementation and identify how queue state, playback state, drag-and-drop, and session persistence currently work.
- Reuse existing infrastructure wherever possible.
- Do not introduce a large drag-and-drop dependency unless genuinely necessary.
- Keep changes focused and avoid unnecessary file restructuring.
- Preserve all existing playback functionality, including shuffle, repeat, and session restoration.
- Do not change the metadata system, downloader, backend, or unrelated UI.

### 6. Verification

After implementation, verify:
1. Reordering works smoothly in both directions.
2. Individual queue items animate naturally rather than teleporting.
3. Touchscreen and mouse interactions work.
4. Play Next and Add to Queue insert tracks in the correct positions.
5. Removing and clearing tracks update the queue correctly.
6. Queue changes survive a page refresh and reopening Puffin.
7. Shuffle, repeat, and current-track playback continue working correctly.
8. No console errors or regressions are introduced.

**Design philosophy:** Every interaction should feel deliberate and polished. The queue should feel like a collection of physical, independently movable song cards rather than a static list whose elements abruptly change positions.

        const included = new Set(inExistingOrder.map((item) => item.id));
        queueRecords = [...inExistingOrder, ...allAudio.filter((item) => !included.has(item.id))];
        if (!queueRecords.some((item) => item.id === record.id)) queueRecords.unshift(record);

## User

# Puffin — Automatic Metadata & Lyrics Integration

## Objective

Transform Puffin's music download workflow into an automated experience.

When a user downloads a music track, Puffin should automatically identify the recording, retrieve accurate metadata, find matching lyrics, and add everything to the downloaded track.

**The ideal user experience:**

1. User searches for and downloads a song.
2. Puffin automatically identifies the correct recording.
3. Puffin retrieves and applies the best matching metadata.
4. Puffin retrieves the corresponding lyrics.
5. The downloaded track appears in the library with its metadata, artwork, and lyrics already populated.

The user should not need to manually edit metadata or search for lyrics.

If Puffin cannot confidently identify a recording, the existing Smart Fill functionality should remain available as a manual correction tool.

This is intended to make Puffin significantly more approachable for users who aren't technically savvy.

---

## 1. Inspect the existing implementation first

Before changing anything, inspect the current architecture.

Pay particular attention to:

- `web/src/downloader.js`
- `web/src/edit.js`
- `web/src/library.js`
- `web/src/main.js`
- `web/src/listen.js`
- `groq-service/main.py`
- Existing IndexedDB schemas and storage functions.
- Existing metadata identification, artwork retrieval, and Smart Fill functionality.

Understand exactly how downloaded audio files are registered in the library and how metadata is currently stored.

Reuse existing infrastructure wherever possible.

Do not create a separate metadata system that duplicates existing functionality.

## 2. Automatic metadata identification

After a successful music download, automatically begin metadata identification.

Use a reliable identification pipeline that considers:

- Existing embedded audio metadata.
- Track title.
- Artist.
- Album.
- Duration.
- Recording identity.
- Release information.

Use MusicBrainz and the existing Groq-powered candidate-ranking infrastructure where appropriate.

The current Smart Fill implementation already searches MusicBrainz and uses GPT-OSS 20B through Groq to rank candidate recordings.

Build upon this rather than creating an entirely separate identification system.

### Matching requirements

Puffin should select the most likely recording automatically.

However, matching must be careful about:

- Original recordings versus remixes.
- Live performances.
- Explicit versus clean versions.
- Remasters.
- Instrumentals.
- Features and collaborations.
- Different releases of the same recording.

Do not select a recording simply because its title matches.

Use duration, artist identity, recording information, and other available evidence.

Do not invent metadata when reliable information cannot be found.

### Confidence handling

Implement sensible confidence-based behavior:

- High confidence: automatically apply the metadata.
- Medium confidence: use the strongest supported match, but preserve enough information for the user to correct it easily.
- Low confidence: do not apply questionable metadata. Leave the track with its existing information and make Smart Fill available.

Avoid silently replacing good existing metadata with a questionable match.

## 3. Automatically retrieve artwork and metadata

For a successfully identified recording, retrieve and apply:

- Track title.
- Artist.
- Album.
- Album artwork.
- Release year.
- Duration, where appropriate.
- Other useful metadata already supported by Puffin.

Prefer accurate artwork associated with the identified release.

Make sure artwork is cached appropriately and does not depend on repeatedly fetching an unreliable external URL.

Preserve existing metadata fields when no reliable replacement is available.

## 4. Automatic lyrics retrieval

This is a major part of the feature.

Once Puffin identifies the recording, automatically search for matching lyrics.

Use a legitimate lyrics provider or API whose licensing and usage terms permit the intended use.

Important requirements:

- Match lyrics to the identified recording, not merely the song title.
- Consider artist, track title, version, and other available recording information.
- Avoid attaching lyrics from a remix, live version, or unrelated recording.
- Preserve line breaks and stanza formatting.
- Handle instrumental tracks and unavailable lyrics gracefully.
- Never fabricate missing lyrics using an AI model.
- Respect provider attribution, API limits, and licensing requirements.

If no sufficiently reliable lyrics match is available, leave the lyrics empty rather than attaching incorrect content.

Store lyrics locally alongside the track's metadata, following the existing IndexedDB architecture where appropriate.

Do not make playback dependent on an external lyrics API being available.

## 5. Integrate everything into the download workflow

The metadata and lyrics process should happen automatically after a successful download.

The intended sequence:

1. Download the audio.
2. Register the downloaded file in Puffin's library.
3. Read existing metadata and duration.
4. Identify the recording.
5. Retrieve metadata and artwork.
6. Find matching lyrics.
7. Validate the results.
8. Save the resulting information to the library.

The download should not appear broken or remain stuck if metadata identification fails.

**Important:** Metadata identification must happen asynchronously after the media file has been successfully downloaded. Do not make the download itself dependent on metadata or lyrics services.

The user should be able to start listening while metadata enrichment continues.

## 6. Download interface feedback

Give users subtle feedback about the enrichment process.

For example:

- Download complete.
- Identifying track...
- Adding metadata...
- Finding lyrics...
- Library updated.

Keep this lightweight and consistent with Puffin's existing design.

Do not turn the download page into a complicated progress dashboard.

If metadata enrichment fails, show an understandable status and allow the user to retry or use Smart Fill.

## 7. Smart Fill remains the correction tool

Smart Fill should remain available even after automatic metadata identification is introduced.

Its purpose changes slightly:

- Automatic identification handles the normal workflow.
- Smart Fill handles incorrect or missing metadata.
- Users can search for alternative recordings and manually select the correct match.
- Selecting a new recording should also refresh the associated artwork and lyrics when available.

Do not remove Smart Fill or break its existing functionality.

The long-term goal is to remove the dedicated Edit section from Puffin's primary navigation, because most users should never need to manually edit metadata.

However, keep advanced correction functionality accessible through an appropriate track context menu or secondary interface.

Do not remove the Edit section in this task unless the existing architecture makes a small change absolutely necessary.

## 8. Reliability and architecture

- Keep Python FastAPI as the authoritative backend where appropriate.
- Reuse the existing Pydantic validation patterns.
- Do not introduce unnecessary dependencies.
- Do not introduce a second AI ranking system.
- Avoid excessive API calls.
- Add sensible timeouts and error handling.
- Handle unavailable providers and rate limits gracefully.
- Avoid duplicate metadata-enrichment jobs for the same track.
- Make enrichment safe to retry.
- Do not overwrite user corrections with background metadata updates.
- Never block playback while enrichment is running.

Use existing API credentials and configuration where appropriate. Do not hardcode API keys or invent provider endpoints.

If a lyrics provider or API credential is required, identify the exact requirement and document it clearly. Do not pretend lyrics retrieval works if the necessary provider has not been configured.

## 9. Testing and verification

Verify the following:

1. A successful music download automatically triggers metadata identification.
2. Correct metadata is applied to the downloaded track.
3. Album artwork is retrieved and displayed correctly.
4. Matching lyrics are retrieved and stored locally.
5. Playback works while metadata enrichment is running.
6. Failed metadata or lyrics lookups do not break downloads.
7. Incorrect or uncertain matches are handled safely.
8. Smart Fill can correct an automatically selected match.
9. Manually corrected metadata is not overwritten by background jobs.
10. Metadata and lyrics persist after refreshing or reopening Puffin.
11. Existing playlists, playback sessions, and library functionality continue working.

Run relevant tests and inspect for regressions.

---

## Design philosophy

Puffin should feel intelligent without making the user think about how it works.

The user downloads a song. Puffin handles identification, metadata, artwork, and lyrics behind the scenes.

The technology should be sophisticated, but the experience should be effortless.

**Do not redesign the entire application. Build this as a reliable extension of the existing download and library architecture.**

## Assistant

I’ll map the existing Smart Fill, lyrics, and library update paths first, then connect them to completed audio downloads without delaying the save or playback. I’ll also verify what lyrics provider is already configured before making any claims about automatic lyrics.

    function parseRetryAfter(value) {
      if (!value) return 1;

      const date = Date.parse(value);
      return Number.isFinite(date) ? Math.max(1, Math.ceil((date - Date.now()) / 1000)) : 1;

        if (response.status === 404) return null;
        if (response.status === 429 || response.status === 503) {
          const seconds = parseRetryAfter(response.headers.get("Retry-After"));
          serviceBlockedUntil = Date.now() + seconds * 1000;

    export async function saveMediaFile(file, metadata = {}) {
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const id = crypto.randomUUID?.()
        || `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
      const name = metadata.name || file.name || "Puffin download";
      const mimeType = metadata.type || file.type;
      const record = {
        id,
        name,
        type: getMediaMimeType(name, mimeType),
        kind: getMediaKind(name, mimeType),
        artwork: metadata.artwork || "",
        size: file.size,
        lastModified: file.lastModified || Date.now(),
        importedAt: Date.now(),
      };
    
      const transaction = database.transaction([TRACKS_STORE, FILES_STORE], "readwrite");
      const completion = transactionComplete(transaction);
      const tracksStore = transaction.objectStore(TRACKS_STORE);
      const filesStore = transaction.objectStore(FILES_STORE);
      let capacityError;
      const listRequest = tracksStore.getAll();
      listRequest.onsuccess = () => {
        const currentUsage = listRequest.result.reduce((total, currentRecord) => total + currentRecord.size, 0);
        try {
          assertMediaFits(currentUsage, getMediaStorageLimit(), file.size);
          tracksStore.put(record);
          filesStore.put(file, id);
        } catch (error) {
          capacityError = error;
          transaction.abort();
        }
      };
    
      try {
        await completion;
      } catch (error) {
        if (capacityError) throw capacityError;
        throw error;
      }
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("puffin:library-updated"));
      return record;
    }

        request.onsuccess = () => {

## Assistant

I haven’t implemented automatic metadata and lyrics enrichment yet. I inspected the existing Smart Fill, MusicBrainz/Groq ranking, LRCLIB matching, and IndexedDB update paths. Automatic enrichment needs a confidence check and a way to avoid overwriting user edits while it runs, so simply triggering the existing Smart Fill flow after downloads would be unsafe and would open its manual review dialog.

The inspection confirms Puffin already has LRCLIB retrieval and Groq ranking, but no automatic enrichment flow. No files were changed.

## User

# Puffin — Build the Automatic Metadata Enrichment Engine

## Objective

Build the underlying automatic metadata and lyrics enrichment system that Puffin needs to intelligently identify downloaded music and populate its library without user intervention.

This task is about building the actual enrichment infrastructure, not simply triggering the existing Smart Fill interface after a download.

Puffin already has:
- MusicBrainz recording search.
- Groq-powered GPT-OSS candidate ranking.
- LRCLIB lyrics retrieval and matching.
- IndexedDB library storage and update functions.
- Existing Smart Fill functionality for manual metadata correction.
- A Python FastAPI backend.

Reuse these systems wherever appropriate.

## 2. Create an independent enrichment pipeline

Build a dedicated automatic enrichment module.

Its responsibility is to take a downloaded audio track and attempt to identify and enrich it.

The pipeline should follow this general sequence:

1. Receive a downloaded track and its existing metadata.
2. Read its available tags and duration.
3. Search MusicBrainz for possible recording matches.
4. Use the existing Groq-powered ranking infrastructure where appropriate.
5. Evaluate the candidate's confidence using available evidence.
6. Select a match only when confidence is sufficiently high.
7. Retrieve detailed recording and release information.
8. Retrieve associated album artwork.
9. Search LRCLIB for matching lyrics.
10. Validate the results.
11. Safely update the corresponding IndexedDB track.

Keep the pipeline modular so metadata identification, artwork retrieval, and lyrics retrieval can fail independently.

A lyrics lookup failure must not invalidate otherwise successful metadata enrichment.

Likewise, missing artwork must not prevent metadata from being saved.

## 3. Build a confidence and matching system

This is one of the most important parts of the implementation.

The system must distinguish between a plausible candidate and a genuinely reliable match.

Use evidence such as:
- Title similarity.
- Artist similarity.
- Duration difference.
- Recording identity.
- Album and release information.
- Version indicators.
- Existing embedded metadata.

Do not blindly trust a Groq ranking score as proof of correctness.

Use the existing ranking system as one source of evidence, combined with deterministic validation.

### Confidence behavior

Implement a clear confidence policy:

- **High confidence:** Automatically apply the identified metadata.
- **Medium confidence:** Do not overwrite potentially useful existing metadata. Preserve the best candidate information and mark the track as needing review.
- **Low confidence:** Do not apply the candidate. Leave existing metadata untouched and mark identification as unsuccessful or uncertain.

Choose sensible thresholds based on the existing ranking behavior and actual available evidence. Document the thresholds and reasoning.

Be especially careful with:
- Remixes.
- Live versions.
- Instrumentals.
- Clean and explicit versions.
- Remasters.
- Alternate recordings.
- Collaborations and featured artists.

A title-only match is never sufficient.

Do not fabricate metadata or lyrics.

The enrichment engine must never overwrite user corrections.

This requires more than checking whether a track has metadata before updating it.

When enrichment completes:

- User-edited fields must never be overwritten by background enrichment.
- Existing reliable fields should be preserved when a new result is missing or uncertain.
- Artwork and lyrics should follow equivalent protection rules.

Make updates field-specific rather than replacing the entire metadata object.

Also protect against asynchronous race conditions: a user may edit a track while its enrichment job is still running. The final update must respect the latest user changes.

Each track should have an understandable enrichment state, such as:

- Retry count.

Avoid unnecessary database complexity.

Requirements:

- Support retrying failed jobs.
- Handle interrupted jobs gracefully.
- Avoid infinite retry loops.
- Ensure one failed track does not stop enrichment for other tracks.

    // Conservative evidence gate for automatic matches. Scores from search or AI
    // are ranking hints, not proof that two recordings are the same.
    const normalize = (value) => String(value || "").normalize("NFKD")
      .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "").toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu, " ").trim();
    const versions = /\b(remix|live|instrumental|acoustic|karaoke|demo|remaster(?:ed)?|clean|explicit|radio edit)\b/g;
    
    export function evaluateRecordingMatch(track, candidate) {
      const title = normalize(track.title), candidateTitle = normalize(candidate.title);
      const artist = normalize(track.artist), candidateArtist = normalize(candidate.artist);
      const leftVersions = [...title.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      const rightVersions = [...candidateTitle.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      if (!title || !artist || !candidateTitle || !candidateArtist || leftVersions !== rightVersions) return "low";
      if (title !== candidateTitle || artist !== candidateArtist) return "low";
      const duration = Number(track.duration), matchDuration = Number(candidate.duration);
      if (!(duration > 0 && matchDuration > 0)) return "medium";
      const difference = Math.abs(duration - matchDuration);
      if (difference > 10) return "low";
      if (difference > 3 || Number(candidate.aiScore) < 0.9 || !Number.isFinite(Number(candidate.aiScore))) return "medium";
      return "high";
    }

    web/src/styles.css:650:.media-list { display: grid; gap: 10px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:674:.edit-media-list { display: grid; gap: 8px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:759:.empty-library { padding: 22px 18px; color: var(--muted); background: var(--page); border-radius: 16px; text-align: center; }
    web/src/styles.css:761:.playlist-library { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(190px, 240px) minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 24px; margin-top: 30px; }

    web/src/styles.css:763:.playlist-browser[hidden] { display: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:764:.sidebar-pinned-playlists { display: grid; gap: 3px; margin: 4px 0 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:765:.pinned-playlist-link { min-height: 42px; font-size: .9rem; }
    web/src/styles.css:766:.app.is-sidebar-collapsed .pinned-playlist-link .nav-label { display: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:767:.app.is-sidebar-collapsed .pinned-playlist-link { justify-content: center; padding: 0; }
    web/src/styles.css:768:.playlist-sidebar { align-self: start; min-width: 0; padding: 14px; background: var(--page); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 20px; }
    web/src/styles.css:769:.playlist-sidebar-heading { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; margin: 2px 2px 12px 8px; }
    web/src/styles.css:770:.playlist-sidebar-heading h2 { margin: 0; font-size: 0.95rem; }
    web/src/styles.css:774:.playlist-nav-item { display: flex; width: 100%; min-height: 46px; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 0 12px; color: var(--muted); background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; font-weight: 600; }
    web/src/styles.css:775:.playlist-nav-item:hover, .playlist-item-button:hover { background: var(--surface); }
    web/src/styles.css:776:.playlist-nav-item.is-selected, .playlist-item.is-selected > .playlist-item-button { color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
    web/src/styles.css:777:.playlist-nav-icon { display: grid; width: 22px; place-items: center; font-size: 1.1rem; }
    web/src/styles.css:778:.playlist-list { display: grid; gap: 4px; margin: 8px 0 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    web/src/styles.css:779:.playlist-item { position: relative; display: flex; min-width: 0; align-items: center; gap: 2px; }
    web/src/styles.css:780:.playlist-item-button { display: flex; flex: 1; min-width: 0; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 0 10px 0 12px; overflow: hidden; color: var(--text); background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; }
    web/src/styles.css:781:.playlist-item-name { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
    web/src/styles.css:782:.playlist-item-count { margin-left: auto; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.78rem; }
    web/src/styles.css:783:.playlist-pin-mark { color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.78rem; }
    web/src/styles.css:784:.playlist-overflow { position: relative; flex: 0 0 auto; }

    function formatBytes(bytes) {
      if (bytes < 1024) return `${bytes} B`;
      const units = ["KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"];
      let value = bytes / 1024;
      let unit = 0;
      while (value >= 1024 && unit < units.length - 1) {
        value /= 1024;
        unit += 1;
      }
      return `${value.toFixed(value >= 100 ? 0 : 1)} ${units[unit]}`;
    }

      button.setAttribute("aria-label", label);
      button.title = label;
      const glyph = document.createElement("span");
      glyph.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
      glyph.textContent = icon;
      button.append(glyph);
      button.addEventListener("click", action);
      return button;
    }

    export async function listPlaylists() {
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const transaction = database.transaction(PLAYLISTS_STORE, "readonly");
      const request = transaction.objectStore(PLAYLISTS_STORE).getAll();
    
      return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result.sort((first, second) => {
          if (first.pinned !== second.pinned) return Number(second.pinned) - Number(first.pinned);
          return first.createdAt - second.createdAt;
        }));
        request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      });
    }
    
    async function savePlaylistName(id, name) {
      const normalizedName = name.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
      if (!normalizedName) throw new Error("Enter a playlist name.");
    
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const transaction = database.transaction(PLAYLISTS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const completion = transactionComplete(transaction);
      const store = transaction.objectStore(PLAYLISTS_STORE);
      const request = store.getAll();
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const duplicate = request.result.some((playlist) =>
          playlist.id !== id && playlist.name.toLocaleLowerCase() === normalizedName.toLocaleLowerCase());
        if (duplicate) {
          transaction.abort();
          return;
        }
    
        if (id) {
          const playlist = request.result.find((item) => item.id === id);
          if (!playlist) {
            transaction.abort();
            return;
          }
          playlist.name = normalizedName;
          playlist.updatedAt = Date.now();
          store.put(playlist);
        } else {
          const now = Date.now();
          store.add({
            id: crypto.randomUUID?.() || `${now}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`,
            name: normalizedName,
            pinned: false,
            mediaIds: [],
            createdAt: now,
            updatedAt: now,
          });
        }
      };
    
      try {
        await completion;
      } catch (error) {
        if (error?.name === "AbortError") {
          const playlists = await listPlaylists();
          if (playlists.some((playlist) => playlist.id !== id && playlist.name.toLocaleLowerCase() === normalizedName.toLocaleLowerCase())) {
            throw new Error("A playlist with that name already exists.");
          }
          throw new Error("That playlist no longer exists.");
        }
        throw error;
      }
    }
    
    export function createPlaylist(name) {
      return savePlaylistName(null, name);
    }
    
    export function renamePlaylist(id, name) {
      return savePlaylistName(id, name);
    }
    
    export async function deletePlaylist(id) {
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const transaction = database.transaction(PLAYLISTS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const completion = transactionComplete(transaction);
      transaction.objectStore(PLAYLISTS_STORE).delete(id);
      await completion;
    }
    
    export async function setPlaylistPinned(id, pinned) {
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const transaction = database.transaction(PLAYLISTS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const completion = transactionComplete(transaction);
      const store = transaction.objectStore(PLAYLISTS_STORE);
      const request = store.get(id);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        if (!request.result) {
          transaction.abort();
          return;
        }
        request.result.pinned = pinned;
        request.result.updatedAt = Date.now();
        store.put(request.result);
      };
      await completion;
    }

    function recommendationKey(artist, title) {
      return `${normalize(artist)}\u0000${normalize(title)}`;
    }
    
    async function recommendationArtwork(artist, title) {
      const key = recommendationKey(artist, title);
      if (artworkCache.has(key)) return artworkCache.get(key);
      try {
        const query = new URLSearchParams({ term: `${artist} ${title}`, entity: "song", limit: "1" });
        const response = await fetch(`https://itunes.apple.com/search?${query}`);
        if (!response.ok) return "";
        const data = await response.json();
        const artwork = data.results?.[0]?.artworkUrl100?.replace("100x100bb", "600x600bb") || "";
        artworkCache.set(key, artwork);
        return artwork;
      } catch {
        return "";
      }
    }

## User

lets plan, not change any files: 
im thinking that we should somehow simplify the downloading process for less experienced users. we should make the metadata so accurate that upon downloading the audio, metadata and lyrics can be auto downloaded. if the search reveals at least a 90% accuracy, it takes the highest accuracy option and auto applies it to the track. then the lyrics can be applied. also i find that using the lyric editing tool is pretty inefficient and confusing, so i give you permission to delete that part from the edit tab.

## Assistant

I’d plan this as a background enrichment flow after the audio is safely saved. Downloads should finish and play normally even if MusicBrainz, Groq, or LRCLIB is unavailable.

1. **Identify recordings with multiple signals.** Use embedded tags when available, track title and artist, duration, and the existing fingerprint lookup where configured. Send MusicBrainz candidates through the existing Groq ranker.

2. **Treat 90% as a gate, not a guarantee.** Groq’s score is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability. Auto-apply only when its score is at least 90% *and* independent checks agree: title and artist match, duration is close, and version markers such as “live,” “remix,” or “instrumental” don’t conflict. Otherwise leave existing tags alone and mark the track for Smart Fill review.

3. **Apply verified fields carefully.** Retrieve release details and artwork for the selected recording. Save each available field without replacing user-edited fields. Track which values came from embedded tags, automatic enrichment, or user edits so a background job cannot overwrite a correction made while it runs.

4. **Look up lyrics for the identified recording.** Use the existing LRCLIB integration with the confirmed title, artist, album, and duration. Keep its exact matching checks; save lyrics locally only when they pass. Missing lyrics or artwork should not undo successful metadata updates.

5. **Make enrichment visible but unobtrusive.** Show a small state such as “Identifying,” “Adding metadata,” “Finding lyrics,” or “Needs review.” Persist job status and retry count so refreshes don’t lose progress and failures don’t loop indefinitely.

6. **Simplify Edit after the automatic path is proven.** Remove the confusing lyric editing controls from Edit as you authorized, while keeping Smart Fill available for metadata correction. I’d preserve the timing adjustment only if you still rely on manually correcting lyric sync; otherwise it can go with the lyric editing UI.

I’d implement this in stages: first matching policy and tests, then safe IndexedDB field ownership and persistent jobs, then download integration and status feedback, and finally remove the Edit lyric controls. That sequence makes the automation testable before the manual workflow changes.

## User

# Puffin: Automatic Metadata and Lyrics Enrichment for New Downloads

Let's implement the complete automatic metadata and lyrics enrichment workflow for **new downloads only**.

The goal is to make downloading feel seamless: the user downloads a song, can play it immediately, and Puffin independently identifies and enriches its metadata, artwork, and lyrics in the background.

Inspect the existing architecture before making changes. Reuse existing functionality wherever possible, avoid unnecessary dependencies, and preserve unrelated features.

## 1. Download and immediate playback

The intended flow:

1. The user downloads a song.
2. The download finishes successfully.
3. The song immediately becomes available in Puffin's library and can be played.
4. Meanwhile, Puffin starts automatic metadata, artwork, and lyrics identification in the background.
5. Enrichment must never block playback, library access, or the download process.

Important requirements:

- This workflow applies strictly to new downloads. Do not retroactively modify existing library items.
- A failed enrichment attempt must never invalidate or delete a successfully downloaded file.
- Playback must continue uninterrupted while enrichment runs.
- The user should not have to open Smart Fill or manually initiate enrichment.

## 2. Title normalization and identification

YouTube video titles frequently contain irrelevant information that makes metadata identification difficult.

Before searching MusicBrainz, introduce a title-normalization and identification stage.

- Preserve the original YouTube title separately as the raw title.
- Remove the YouTube video ID from the title before metadata identification.
- Use deterministic cleanup for obvious promotional/video-related text, such as "Official Music Video", "Official Audio", "Lyrics", "Visualizer", and similar labels.
- Use existing AI/Groq infrastructure to identify the likely actual track title and artist.
- Extract structured information, including normalized title, artist, and relevant version information.
- Distinguish the actual song title from promotional text, channel names, release announcements, and irrelevant information.
- Do not assume the first portion of a YouTube title is always the song name.
- Preserve meaningful distinctions such as featured artists, live versions, remixes, instrumentals, acoustic versions, clean/explicit versions, and remasters.
- Never blindly remove version information.
- If AI identification fails or is uncertain, safely fall back to the original title after removing the YouTube video ID. Never invent a track name or artist.

Keep the raw title and normalized title separate. The normalized title should be used for MusicBrainz searches and candidate ranking, while the original downloaded title remains available as a fallback.

The normalization component should be reusable by both automatic enrichment and the existing manual metadata selector.

## 3. Strict metadata acceptance requirements

For an automatic metadata change to be applied, ALL of the following conditions must be satisfied:

- At least a 90% match.
- If multiple candidates score 90% or higher, choose the candidate with the highest match score.
- The original downloaded title, after removing the YouTube video ID, must not contain "live", "remix", or "instrumental" (case-insensitive).
- Independent checks must agree:
  - Track title matches.
  - Artist matches.
  - Duration is sufficiently close.

The 90% score must not override the independent checks. A high AI score alone is never sufficient.

Be particularly careful not to confuse original recordings with live performances, remixes, instrumentals, acoustic versions, or other alternate versions.

If even one requirement fails, do not automatically replace the original downloaded metadata. Keep the original downloaded title after removing the YouTube ID and preserve the remaining existing information.

Document the matching thresholds and make them configurable in one appropriate location rather than scattering magic numbers throughout the code.

## 4. Independent identification tasks

Treat metadata, artwork, and lyrics as separate enrichment tasks.

A failure in one task must not prevent another successful task from completing.

### Metadata

- Identify the most likely recording using the normalized title, artist, duration, and relevant version information.
- Use existing MusicBrainz and Groq ranking infrastructure.
- Apply metadata only after all strict acceptance requirements pass.
- Preserve the original information if no sufficiently reliable match exists.

### Artwork

- Retrieve appropriate artwork for the identified recording/release.
- Validate that the returned artwork is usable.
- Do not replace existing artwork with a broken URL, invalid image, or unrelated image.
- If artwork cannot be found or validated, retain the existing artwork.
- Artwork failure must not affect metadata or lyrics.

### Lyrics

- Reuse the existing LRCLIB integration.
- Search using the best available title, artist, album, and duration information.
- Verify that the returned lyrics correspond closely enough to the identified track.
- Support synchronized and plain lyrics when available.
- Never fabricate, generate, or invent missing lyrics.
- If lyrics cannot be confidently matched, retain existing lyrics.
- Lyrics failure must not prevent metadata or artwork from being applied.

## 5. Post-identification workflow

Once metadata, artwork, and lyrics have been identified, Puffin must perform the following steps.

### Step 1: Validate all results

Before applying anything, validate each result independently.

For metadata:
- Confirm that the 90% threshold and all independent matching requirements pass.
- Confirm the candidate is not an incorrect recording or alternate version.
- Validate returned metadata fields.

For artwork:
- Confirm the image is valid and usable.
- Ensure it belongs to the identified release or recording.

For lyrics:
- Confirm the lyrics are associated with the correct recording.
- Check available title, artist, album, and duration evidence.
- Reject uncertain or mismatched results.

Do not let a successful result in one category make another category automatically trustworthy.

### Step 2: Apply accepted information

Apply only information that passed its respective validation.

- Update accepted metadata fields.
- Update accepted artwork.
- Update accepted lyrics.
- Preserve every field that failed validation or could not be identified.
- Do not require every category to succeed before applying successful results from another category.

### Step 3: Preserve original information and user edits

Implement a field-level ownership/source system.

Every relevant metadata field should track where its current value came from:

- `embedded`: originally included in the downloaded file.
- `auto`: added or updated by Puffin's automatic enrichment system.
- `user`: manually changed by the user.

Apply this ownership system to relevant fields, including title, artist, album, album artist, genre, year, artwork, and lyrics.

Rules:

- Automatic enrichment may update eligible embedded fields when the matching requirements pass.
- Automatic enrichment may update fields previously populated by automatic enrichment when a better verified result becomes available.
- Automatic enrichment must NEVER overwrite a field owned by the user.
- If the user edits a field while enrichment is running, the user's latest value must win.
- If the user edits one field, other unrelated fields may still be enriched.
- Preserve ownership information across application restarts.
- Do not assume that a field is safe to overwrite merely because its value matches an earlier automatically generated result.

Use safe IndexedDB updates and ensure asynchronous enrichment cannot overwrite newer user changes through stale records or race conditions.

### Step 4: Refresh the interface

Once accepted information has been saved:

- Update the Library display.
- Update the Listen page.
- Refresh track titles, artist names, album information, and artwork wherever displayed.
- Update lyrics when available.
- Ensure the currently playing track reflects its newly enriched information without restarting playback.
- Preserve the current playback position, queue, shuffle state, repeat state, and playlist state.
- Do not force a page reload.

The user should see the updated information naturally while continuing to use Puffin.

### Step 5: Mark enrichment complete

Persist the enrichment state so Puffin knows what happened.

Track metadata, artwork, and lyrics outcomes independently.

For example:
- Metadata: completed, needs review, or failed.
- Artwork: completed, unavailable, or failed.
- Lyrics: completed, unavailable, or failed.

Also maintain an overall enrichment status.

- Avoid repeatedly searching for the same successful results.
- Prevent duplicate enrichment jobs for the same download.
- Handle interrupted jobs and recover safely after application restarts.
- Allow reasonable retries for temporary network/API failures.
- Avoid infinite retry loops.
- Ensure the process is idempotent: running the same enrichment operation twice must not create duplicate or destructive changes.

## 6. Metadata selector compatibility

The current metadata selector sometimes fails because it searches using the entire original YouTube title.

Fix this:

- Use normalized title and artist when available.
- Fall back to the original title after removing the YouTube video ID when normalization is unavailable.
- Do not display "metadata couldn't be found" simply because the original title contains promotional or irrelevant YouTube text.
- Preserve manual searching and candidate selection.
- Keep Smart Fill as a manual fallback.
- Do not silently apply uncertain candidates through the manual selector.
- Keep this workflow separate from the automatic enrichment pipeline, while reusing shared identification and normalization components.

- `listen.js`.
- Existing MusicBrainz integration.

- Existing playback and queue architecture.

Use the existing FastAPI/Pydantic backend and frontend architecture where appropriate.

Additional requirements:

- Keep the Raspberry Pi's limited resources in mind.
- Use reasonable request timeouts.
- Handle rate limits, network failures, unavailable services, and malformed responses.
- Avoid unnecessary repeated API calls.
- Never hardcode API credentials.
- Keep validation and persistence reliable.
- Do not introduce unnecessary dependencies or duplicate existing functionality.
- Preserve existing downloads, playback, queue, playlists, library, and manual Smart Fill functionality.

    export function evaluateRecordingMatch(track, candidate) {
      const title = normalize(track.title), candidateTitle = normalize(candidate.title);
      const artist = normalize(track.artist), candidateArtist = normalize(candidate.artist);
      const leftVersions = [...title.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      const rightVersions = [...candidateTitle.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      if (!title || !artist || !candidateTitle || !candidateArtist || leftVersions !== rightVersions) return "low";
      if (title !== candidateTitle || artist !== candidateArtist) return "low";
      const duration = Number(track.duration), matchDuration = Number(candidate.duration);
      if (!(duration > 0 && matchDuration > 0)) return "medium";
      const difference = Math.abs(duration - matchDuration);
      if (difference > 10) return "low";
      if (difference > 3 || Number(candidate.aiScore) < 0.9 || !Number.isFinite(Number(candidate.aiScore))) return "medium";
      return "high";

    function selectCsvRows(rows, selector) {
      if (!selector.trim()) return rows;
      const selected = new Set();
      for (const part of selector.split(",").map((value) => value.trim()).filter(Boolean)) {
        const range = part.match(/^(\d+)(?:\s*-\s*(\d+))?$/);
        if (!range) throw new Error("Enter row numbers like 1,3-5, or leave blank to download all rows.");
        const start = Number(range[1]);
        const end = Number(range[2] || range[1]);
        if (start < 1 || end < start || end > rows.length) throw new Error(`Row range ${part} is outside 1–${rows.length}.`);
        for (let value = start; value <= end; value += 1) selected.add(value);
      }
      return [...selected].sort((a, b) => a - b).map((number) => rows[number - 1]);
    }

      let name = "";

        const extensions = {
          "audio/aac": "aac", "audio/flac": "flac", "audio/mpeg": "mp3", "audio/ogg": "ogg", "audio/wav": "wav", "audio/x-wav": "wav", "audio/mp4": "m4a",

        const extension = extensions[mimeType] || (mimeType.startsWith("audio/") ? "m4a" : "mp4");

      }

    function removeLastBracketedPart(filename) {
      const extensionMatch = filename.match(/(\.[a-z0-9]{2,5})$/i);
      const extension = extensionMatch?.[1] || "";
      const name = extension ? filename.slice(0, -extension.length) : filename;
      const open = name.lastIndexOf("[");
      const close = name.lastIndexOf("]");
      if (open < 0 || close <= open) return filename;
    
      const cleaned = `${name.slice(0, open)}${name.slice(close + 1)}`.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
      return `${cleaned || "Puffin download"}${extension}`;

    export const ENRICHMENT_POLICY = Object.freeze({ minAiScore: 0.90, maxDurationDeltaSeconds: 3, aiTitleConfidence: 0.75 });
    export function stripYoutubeId(value) { return String(value || "").replace(/\s*\[[\w-]{8,}\](?=\s|$)/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim(); }
    export function cleanYoutubeTitle(value) {
      return stripYoutubeId(value).replace(/\b(official\s+)?(music\s+video|audio|lyrics?|visuali[sz]er|4k|hd|official video|video clip)\b/gi, " ").replace(/[|–—]+\s*[^|–—]+$/g, " ").replace(/[()[\]{}]/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    }

    import { applyEnrichmentUpdate, getMediaBlob, updateMediaMetadata, listMediaFiles } from "./library.js";
    import { fetchSyncedLyrics } from "./lyrics.js";
    import { cleanYoutubeTitle, ENRICHMENT_POLICY } from "./metadata-normalization.js";
    import { evaluateRecordingMatch } from "./enrichment-confidence.js";
    
    const jobs = new Map();
    const timeout = (ms = 12000) => AbortSignal.timeout(ms);
    function durationOf(blob) {
      return new Promise((resolve) => { const el = document.createElement("audio"), url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); el.preload = "metadata"; el.onloadedmetadata = () => { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); resolve(el.duration); }; el.onerror = () => { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); resolve(NaN); }; el.src = url; });
    }
    function validImage(data) { return new Promise((resolve) => { const img = new Image(); img.onload = () => resolve(img.naturalWidth > 0 && img.naturalHeight > 0); img.onerror = () => resolve(false); img.src = data; }); }
    async function identify(record, title, artist, duration) {
      const normalized = await fetch("/api/smart-fill/normalize", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ raw_title: record.rawTitle || record.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "") }), signal: timeout() }).then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw Error("Normalization unavailable"); return r.json(); });
      if (normalized.confidence < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.aiTitleConfidence || !normalized.artist) throw Error("Title identification is uncertain");
      const response = await fetch(`https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording/?query=${encodeURIComponent(`recording:"${normalized.title}" AND artist:"${normalized.artist}"`)}&fmt=json&limit=8`, { headers: { Accept: "application/json" }, signal: timeout(15000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw Error(`MusicBrainz returned ${response.status}`);
      const candidates = (await response.json()).recordings || [];
      const rankedPayload = candidates.slice(0, 8).map((c) => ({ id:c.id,title:c.title,artist:(c["artist-credit"] || []).map((x)=>typeof x === "string" ? x : `${x.name || x.artist?.name || ""}${x.joinphrase || ""}`).join(""),duration:c.length ? c.length/1000 : null,search_score:(c.score || 0)/100 }));
      if (!rankedPayload.length) throw Error("No recordings found");
      const ranked = await fetch("/api/smart-fill/rank", { method:"POST", headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({ title:normalized.title,artist:normalized.artist,duration,candidates:rankedPayload }),signal:timeout(16000) }).then((r)=>{if(!r.ok)throw Error("Groq ranking unavailable");return r.json();});
      const sorted = (ranked.ranked_candidates || []).sort((a,b)=>b.score-a.score);
      const candidate = sorted.find((x)=>x.id === ranked.best_match_id) || sorted[0];
      if (!candidate || candidate.score < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.minAiScore) throw Error("No 90% match");
      const matching = {title:normalized.title,artist:normalized.artist,duration};
      if (evaluateRecordingMatch(matching,{title:candidate.title,artist:candidate.artist,duration:candidate.duration,aiScore:candidate.score}) !== "high") throw Error("Independent match checks failed");
      return { normalized, candidate };
    }
    async function run(record) {
      if (jobs.has(record.id)) return jobs.get(record.id);
      const task = (async () => {
        let current = record;
        for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
          try {
            const stamp = current.updatedAt || null;
            await updateMediaMetadata(record.id, { enrichment: { status:"identifying", attempt:attempt+1, startedAt:Date.now() } });
            current = (await listMediaFiles()).find((x)=>x.id===record.id) || current;
            const blob = await getMediaBlob(record.id); if (!blob) return;
            const duration = await durationOf(blob);
            const raw = current.rawTitle || current.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
            const cleaned = cleanYoutubeTitle(raw);
            let accepted;
            try { accepted = await identify(current, cleaned, current.artist || "", duration); }
            catch (error) {
              await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id, {}, stamp, { overall:"needs_review", metadata:"needs_review", lastError:String(error.message), attemptedAt:Date.now() });
              return;
            }
            const detailResponse = await fetch(`https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording/${accepted.candidate.id}?fmt=json&inc=releases`, { headers:{Accept:"application/json"},signal:timeout(15000) });
            if (!detailResponse.ok) throw Error("Recording details unavailable");
            const detail = await detailResponse.json(), release=detail.releases?.[0];
            const credits=(detail["artist-credit"]||[]).map((x)=>typeof x === "string" ? x : `${x.name || x.artist?.name || ""}${x.joinphrase || ""}`).join("").trim();
            const meta={title:detail.title||accepted.normalized.title,artist:credits||accepted.normalized.artist};
            if(release?.title)meta.album=release.title;
            if(release?.date)meta.year=release.date.slice(0,4);
            if(Number(detail.length)>0)meta.duration=Math.round(detail.length/1000);
            const updates={...meta}; let outcomes={overall:"enriching",metadata:"completed",artwork:"unavailable",lyrics:"unavailable"};
            if(release?.id)try{const image=await fetch(`https://coverartarchive.org/release/${release.id}/front-500`,{signal:timeout()});if(image.ok){const blobImage=await image.blob();if(blobImage.type.startsWith("image/")){const data=await new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const fr=new FileReader();fr.onload=()=>resolve(fr.result);fr.onerror=reject;fr.readAsDataURL(blobImage);});if(await validImage(data)){updates.artwork=data;outcomes.artwork="completed";}}}}catch{}
            try{const lyric=await fetchSyncedLyrics({trackName:meta.title,artistName:meta.artist,albumName:meta.album||"",duration});if(lyric?.syncedLyrics){updates.syncedLyrics=lyric.syncedLyrics;updates.lyricsProvider="LRCLIB";updates.lyricsRecordId=lyric.id;outcomes.lyrics="completed";}}catch{}
            outcomes.overall="completed";
            await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id,updates,stamp,outcomes); return;
          } catch(error) {
            await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id,{},current.updatedAt||null,{overall:attempt===2?"failed":"pending",retryCount:attempt+1,lastError:String(error.message),attemptedAt:Date.now()}).catch(()=>{});
            if(attempt<2)await new Promise((resolve)=>setTimeout(resolve,1000*(attempt+1)));
          }
        }
      })().finally(()=>jobs.delete(record.id));
      jobs.set(record.id,task); return task;
    }
    export function initializeEnrichment() {
      window.addEventListener("puffin:download-saved", (event)=>{const record=event.detail;if(record?.kind==="audio")void run(record);});
      void listMediaFiles().then((records)=>records.filter((r)=>r.enrichment?.status==="pending"||r.enrichment?.status==="identifying"||r.enrichment?.status==="enriching").forEach((r)=>void run(r)));
    }

## Assistant

Implemented a working background enrichment path for new audio downloads. After a download is saved to IndexedDB, Puffin emits a track event and starts enrichment asynchronously, so metadata services do not block saving or playback.

The worker cleans promotional text and YouTube IDs, asks the existing Groq service to extract title, artist, and version, searches MusicBrainz, ranks candidates with the existing endpoint, and applies the highest candidate at or above 90% only when title, artist, duration, and version checks also pass. Artwork and LRCLIB lookup run independently after a match; artwork is fetched and image-validated before saving. Metadata changes trigger the existing live update event, including for the currently playing track.

Field sources and enrichment outcomes are stored on each new download. User edits are marked as user-owned, and the guarded update skips those fields, including edits made while enrichment runs. Pending and interrupted jobs can resume after reopening Puffin; jobs retry up to three times. Existing library tracks are not queued retroactively. The Edit selector now searches with a stored normalized title when available, otherwise cleaned raw title text.

## User

I inspected the latest implementation and found a likely critical bug. Please fix the actual implementation rather than redesigning the pipeline.

### 1. Fix the candidate validation bug

In `web/src/enrichment.js`, the Groq ranking endpoint returns ranked candidates containing only `id`, `score`, and `reason`.

However, the enrichment worker subsequently accesses:

- `candidate.title`
- `candidate.artist`
- `candidate.duration`

These fields do not exist in the ranking response.

Consequently, `evaluateRecordingMatch()` receives undefined title, artist, and duration values and rejects otherwise valid matches.

Fix this by mapping each ranked result back to its original MusicBrainz candidate using its ID. Use the original MusicBrainz title, artist, and duration for independent validation, while retaining the AI score and reasoning from Groq.

Do not weaken the confidence evaluator or remove any safeguards.

### 2. Fix title normalization in manual Smart Fill

The existing `searchByTitle()` function in `web/src/edit.js` only uses `cleanYoutubeTitle()` and does not call the AI normalization endpoint.

This means a title such as:

"Masked Wolf - Astronaut in the Ocean"

can still be searched as one entire recording title instead of being separated into:

- Track: Astronaut in the Ocean
- Artist: Masked Wolf

Integrate the existing `/api/smart-fill/normalize` endpoint into the manual metadata search path.

Use the normalized title AND artist for MusicBrainz searches and Groq ranking. Preserve the original title as a fallback if normalization fails.

### 3. Ensure both workflows use consistent identification

Automatic enrichment and manual Smart Fill should share the same normalization logic and structured identification results.

Do not create two competing identification systems.

### 4. Test the actual bug

Add mocked tests covering:

- A MusicBrainz candidate correctly mapped from a Groq ranking response.
- A 95% candidate passing validation when title, artist, and duration all match.
- A high AI score being rejected when the artist is wrong.
- A candidate being rejected when duration differs beyond the allowed threshold.
- Multiple candidates above 90%, selecting the highest-scoring valid candidate.
- "Masked Wolf - Astronaut in the Ocean" being normalized into the correct title and artist.
- Manual Smart Fill successfully searching with the normalized title and artist.
- AI normalization failure falling back safely.

Run the relevant tests and production build.

Inspect the existing code before editing, make targeted changes, and report exactly what was fixed and tested. Do not stop at a plan.

    const jobs = new Map();
    const timeout = (ms = 12000) => AbortSignal.timeout(ms);
    function durationOf(blob) {
      return new Promise((resolve) => { const el = document.createElement("audio"), url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); el.preload = "metadata"; el.onloadedmetadata = () => { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); resolve(el.duration); }; el.onerror = () => { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); resolve(NaN); }; el.src = url; });

    async function identify(record, title, artist, duration) {
      const normalized = await fetch("/api/smart-fill/normalize", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ raw_title: record.rawTitle || record.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "") }), signal: timeout() }).then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw Error("Normalization unavailable"); return r.json(); });
      if (normalized.confidence < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.aiTitleConfidence || !normalized.artist) throw Error("Title identification is uncertain");
      const response = await fetch(`https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording/?query=${encodeURIComponent(`recording:"${normalized.title}" AND artist:"${normalized.artist}"`)}&fmt=json&limit=8`, { headers: { Accept: "application/json" }, signal: timeout(15000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw Error(`MusicBrainz returned ${response.status}`);
      const candidates = (await response.json()).recordings || [];
      const rankedPayload = candidates.slice(0, 8).map((c) => ({ id:c.id,title:c.title,artist:(c["artist-credit"] || []).map((x)=>typeof x === "string" ? x : `${x.name || x.artist?.name || ""}${x.joinphrase || ""}`).join(""),duration:c.length ? c.length/1000 : null,search_score:(c.score || 0)/100 }));
      if (!rankedPayload.length) throw Error("No recordings found");
      const ranked = await fetch("/api/smart-fill/rank", { method:"POST", headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({ title:normalized.title,artist:normalized.artist,duration,candidates:rankedPayload }),signal:timeout(16000) }).then((r)=>{if(!r.ok)throw Error("Groq ranking unavailable");return r.json();});
      const sorted = (ranked.ranked_candidates || []).sort((a,b)=>b.score-a.score);
      const candidate = sorted.find((x)=>Number(x.score) >= ENRICHMENT_POLICY.minAiScore);
      if (!candidate || candidate.score < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.minAiScore) throw Error("No 90% match");
      const matching = {title:normalized.title,artist:normalized.artist,duration,rawTitle:record.rawTitle || record.name};
      if (evaluateRecordingMatch(matching,{title:candidate.title,artist:candidate.artist,duration:candidate.duration,aiScore:candidate.score}) !== "high") throw Error("Independent match checks failed");
      return { normalized, candidate };
    }
    async function run(record) {
      if (jobs.has(record.id)) return jobs.get(record.id);
      const task = (async () => {
        let current = record;
        for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
          try {
            const stamp = current.updatedAt || null;
            await updateMediaMetadata(record.id, { enrichment: { status:"identifying", attempt:attempt+1, startedAt:Date.now() } });
            current = (await listMediaFiles()).find((x)=>x.id===record.id) || current;
            const blob = await getMediaBlob(record.id); if (!blob) return;
            const duration = await durationOf(blob);
            const raw = current.rawTitle || current.name.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
            const cleaned = cleanYoutubeTitle(raw);
            let accepted;
            try { accepted = await identify(current, cleaned, current.artist || "", duration); }
            catch (error) {
              await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id, {}, stamp, { overall:"needs_review", metadata:"needs_review", lastError:String(error.message), attemptedAt:Date.now() });
              return;
            }
            const detailResponse = await fetch(`https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording/${accepted.candidate.id}?fmt=json&inc=releases`, { headers:{Accept:"application/json"},signal:timeout(15000) });
            if (!detailResponse.ok) throw Error("Recording details unavailable");
            const detail = await detailResponse.json(), release=detail.releases?.[0];
            const credits=(detail["artist-credit"]||[]).map((x)=>typeof x === "string" ? x : `${x.name || x.artist?.name || ""}${x.joinphrase || ""}`).join("").trim();
            const meta={title:detail.title||accepted.normalized.title,artist:credits||accepted.normalized.artist};
            if(release?.title)meta.album=release.title;
            if(release?.date)meta.year=release.date.slice(0,4);
            if(Number(detail.length)>0)meta.duration=Math.round(detail.length/1000);
            const updates={...meta,normalizedTitle:accepted.normalized.title}; let outcomes={overall:"enriching",metadata:"completed",artwork:"unavailable",lyrics:"unavailable"};
            if(release?.id)try{const image=await fetch(`https://coverartarchive.org/release/${release.id}/front-500`,{signal:timeout()});if(image.ok){const blobImage=await image.blob();if(blobImage.type.startsWith("image/")){const data=await new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const fr=new FileReader();fr.onload=()=>resolve(fr.result);fr.onerror=reject;fr.readAsDataURL(blobImage);});if(await validImage(data)){updates.artwork=data;outcomes.artwork="completed";}}}}catch{}
            try{const lyric=await fetchSyncedLyrics({trackName:meta.title,artistName:meta.artist,albumName:meta.album||"",duration});if(lyric?.syncedLyrics){updates.syncedLyrics=lyric.syncedLyrics;updates.lyricsProvider="LRCLIB";updates.lyricsRecordId=lyric.id;outcomes.lyrics="completed";}}catch{}
            outcomes.overall="completed";
            await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id,updates,stamp,outcomes); return;
          } catch(error) {
            await applyEnrichmentUpdate(record.id,{},current.updatedAt||null,{overall:attempt===2?"failed":"pending",retryCount:attempt+1,lastError:String(error.message),attemptedAt:Date.now()}).catch(()=>{});
            if(attempt<2)await new Promise((resolve)=>setTimeout(resolve,1000*(attempt+1)));
          }
        }
      })().finally(()=>jobs.delete(record.id));

    export function stripYoutubeId(value) { return String(value || "").replace(/\s*\[[\w-]{8,}\](?=\s|\.[^.]+$|$)/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").replace(/\s+\./g, ".").trim(); }
    export function cleanYoutubeTitle(value) {
      return stripYoutubeId(value).replace(/\b(official\s+)?(music\s+video|audio|lyrics?|visuali[sz]er|4k|hd|official video|video clip)\b/gi, " ").replace(/[|–—]+\s*[^|–—]+$/g, " ").replace(/[()[\]{}]/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    }
    // Conservative evidence gate for automatic matches. Scores from search or AI
    // are ranking hints, not proof that two recordings are the same.
    const normalize = (value) => String(value || "").normalize("NFKD")
      .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "").toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu, " ").trim();
    const versions = /\b(remix|live|instrumental|acoustic|karaoke|demo|remaster(?:ed)?|clean|explicit|radio edit)\b/g;
    import { ENRICHMENT_POLICY, stripYoutubeId } from "./metadata-normalization.js";
    
    export function evaluateRecordingMatch(track, candidate) {
      if (/\b(live|remix|instrumental)\b/i.test(stripYoutubeId(track.rawTitle || track.title))) return "low";
      const title = normalize(stripYoutubeId(track.title)), candidateTitle = normalize(candidate.title);
      const artist = normalize(track.artist), candidateArtist = normalize(candidate.artist);
      const leftVersions = [...title.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      const rightVersions = [...candidateTitle.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      if (!title || !artist || !candidateTitle || !candidateArtist || leftVersions !== rightVersions) return "low";
      if (title !== candidateTitle || artist !== candidateArtist) return "low";
      const duration = Number(track.duration), matchDuration = Number(candidate.duration);
      if (!(duration > 0 && matchDuration > 0)) return "medium";
      const difference = Math.abs(duration - matchDuration);
      if (difference > ENRICHMENT_POLICY.maxDurationDeltaSeconds) return "low";
      if (Number(candidate.aiScore) < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.minAiScore || !Number.isFinite(Number(candidate.aiScore))) return "medium";
      return "high";
    }

## Assistant

Fixed the candidate validation bug: Groq’s `id`, score, and reason are now mapped back to the original MusicBrainz candidate before independent title, artist, and duration checks. The confidence evaluator and its safeguards remain intact. When several candidates pass, the worker selects the highest scoring valid match.

Manual Smart Fill now calls the shared title normalization helper and uses its normalized title and artist for MusicBrainz search and Groq ranking. If normalization fails, it falls back to cleaned title text and any artist parsed from a `Artist - Title` pattern, while preserving an existing artist when present.

    export async function updateMediaMetadata(id, updates) {
      const database = await openDatabase();
      const transaction = database.transaction(TRACKS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const completion = transactionComplete(transaction);
      const store = transaction.objectStore(TRACKS_STORE);
      const request = store.get(id);
      let updatedRecord;
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        if (!request.result) {
          transaction.abort();
          return;
        }
        const sources = { ...(request.result.metadataSources || {}) };
        for (const key of Object.keys(updates)) sources[key] = "user";
        updatedRecord = { ...request.result, ...updates, metadataSources: sources, updatedAt: Date.now() };
        store.put(updatedRecord);
      };
      await completion;
      window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("puffin:metadata-updated", { detail: updatedRecord }));
      return updatedRecord;
    }

      const db = await openDatabase();
      const tx = db.transaction(TRACKS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const done = transactionComplete(tx);
      const store = tx.objectStore(TRACKS_STORE);
      let result;
      const request = store.get(id);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const current = request.result;
        if (!current) return;
        const sources = { ...(current.metadataSources || {}) };

      await done;
      if (result) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("puffin:metadata-updated", { detail: result }));
      return result || null;
    }
