    export function evaluateRecordingMatch(track, candidate) {
      if (/\b(live|remix|instrumental)\b/i.test(stripYoutubeId(track.rawTitle || track.title))) return "low";
      const title = normalize(stripYoutubeId(track.title)), candidateTitle = normalize(candidate.title);
      const artist = normalize(track.artist), candidateArtist = normalize(candidate.artist);
      const leftVersions = [...title.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      const rightVersions = [...candidateTitle.matchAll(versions)].map((item) => item[0]).sort().join("|");
      if (!title || !artist || !candidateTitle || !candidateArtist || leftVersions !== rightVersions) return "low";
      if (title !== candidateTitle || artist !== candidateArtist) return "low";
      const duration = Number(track.duration), matchDuration = Number(candidate.duration);
      if (!(duration > 0 && matchDuration > 0)) return "medium";
      const difference = Math.abs(duration - matchDuration);
      if (difference > ENRICHMENT_POLICY.maxDurationDeltaSeconds) return "low";
      if (Number(candidate.aiScore) < ENRICHMENT_POLICY.minAiScore || !Number.isFinite(Number(candidate.aiScore))) return "medium";
      return "high";
    }

        const original = byId.get(ranked.id);
        return original ? [{ ...original, aiScore: ranked.score, aiReason: ranked.reason }] : [];
      }).sort((a, b) => b.aiScore - a.aiScore);
    }

## Assistant

I found and fixed a concrete reason automatic enrichment could fail while Smart Fill worked: if Groq title normalization failed or timed out, the automatic worker stopped instead of searching with the cleaned title. It now falls back to the cleaned artist and title, then uses the same MusicBrainz search as Smart Fill. The 90% score and independent match checks remain.

I also gave Groq more time and output space. The red status circle now shows the saved error when you hover over it, which will help identify any remaining failure.

All 28 frontend tests and the production build passed. I can’t confirm this was the cause of your particular download without its saved error; the tests used mocked services. Deploy the changes and try a **new** download—the existing failed track won’t retry automatically.

how do we find the saved error?

## Assistant

Open **Edit** and find the red status dot beside **Smart Fill** for the downloaded track. Hover over it with a mouse to see the saved error.

On a phone, the dot’s tooltip may not appear. If so, open Puffin in a desktop browser and hover over the dot. The error is saved with that track’s enrichment status in IndexedDB, but the app doesn’t currently show it in a tap-friendly message.

## Assistant

The saved message hid the HTTP response, so **“Groq ranking unavailable” did not reveal the exact server rejection**. Comparing the requests exposed a concrete mismatch: automatic enrichment sent up to eight candidates with unsliced title and artist fields, while Smart Fill sends at most six and truncates those fields to the limits expected by the FastAPI request model. An oversized MusicBrainz result could therefore make automatic ranking fail validation even when Smart Fill succeeds.

I aligned the automatic request with Smart Fill’s candidate count and field limits, while keeping full MusicBrainz data for independent validation. The status now includes the HTTP status and response detail if ranking fails again.

All 28 frontend tests and the production build passed. The payload fix is implemented, though I have not verified it against your live download. After deploying, try a new download; if it still fails, the status should show the server response that was previously hidden.

    function getFingerprintWorker() {

    async function fingerprintSamples(buffer) {
      const frameLimit = Math.min(buffer.length, Math.floor(buffer.sampleRate * FINGERPRINT_LIMIT_SECONDS));

## Assistant

The MusicBrainz 503 is a direct explanation for the failed metadata lookup. I found why it stayed failed: the worker treated every identification error as a permanent “needs review” result, so a temporary 503 bypassed its retry loop. I’m changing that so service errors can retry; the WASM errors are a separate fingerprinting issue.

## Assistant

That message narrows it down: enrichment got as far as requesting Groq’s candidate ranking, then that request failed. It does **not** reveal why Groq failed. The cause could be a missing `GROQ_API_KEY`, a Groq service error, or a rejected request. The WASM errors are separate and aren’t the cause of this ranking failure.

I updated the error handling so ranking failures are saved with the HTTP status and response details, and temporary ranking or MusicBrainz errors are retried instead of immediately being marked for review. After deploying this change, a new attempt should show a more specific error if ranking fails again. The existing saved error won’t gain those details retroactively.

The changes are in [enrichment.js](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/web/src/enrichment.js) and [metadata-normalization.js](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/web/src/metadata-normalization.js). All 28 frontend tests passed, and the production build passed.

    export const ENRICHMENT_POLICY = Object.freeze({ minAiScore: 0.90, maxDurationDeltaSeconds: 3, aiTitleConfidence: 0.75 });
    export function stripYoutubeId(value) { return String(value || "").replace(/\s*\[[\w-]{8,}\](?=\s|\.[^.]+$|$)/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").replace(/\s+\./g, ".").trim(); }
    export function cleanYoutubeTitle(value) {
      return stripYoutubeId(value).replace(/\b(official\s+)?(music\s+video|audio|lyrics?|visuali[sz]er|4k|hd|official video|video clip)\b/gi, " ").replace(/[|–—]+\s*[^|–—]+$/g, " ").replace(/[()[\]{}]/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    }
    
    export async function normalizeTrackTitle(rawTitle, fetcher = fetch) {
      const cleaned = cleanYoutubeTitle(rawTitle);
      const split = cleaned.match(/^(.+?)\s+[-–—]\s+(.+)$/);
      const fallback = { title: split?.[2]?.trim() || cleaned, artist: split?.[1]?.trim() || "", version: "", confidence: 0 };
      try {

    export async function applyEnrichmentUpdate(id, updates, expectedUpdatedAt, outcomes) {
      const db = await openDatabase();
      const tx = db.transaction(TRACKS_STORE, "readwrite");
      const done = transactionComplete(tx);
      const store = tx.objectStore(TRACKS_STORE);
      let result;
      const request = store.get(id);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const current = request.result;
        if (!current) return;
        const sources = { ...(current.metadataSources || {}) };
        const accepted = {};
        for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(updates)) {
          if (value == null || value === "" || sources[field] === "user") continue;
          if ((current.updatedAt || null) !== (expectedUpdatedAt || null) && !sources[field]) continue;
          accepted[field] = value;
          sources[field] = "auto";
        }
        result = { ...current, ...accepted, metadataSources: sources,
          enrichment: { ...(current.enrichment || {}), ...outcomes, updatedAt: Date.now() } };
        store.put(result);
      };
      await done;
      if (result) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("puffin:metadata-updated", { detail: result }));
      return result || null;
    }

## Assistant

The 503 confirms MusicBrainz itself is returning “Service Unavailable.” That is an upstream response, not a title-matching failure. The previous retry policy gave up quickly and turned the status red.

I updated the MusicBrainz request path to serialize requests in the tab, honor `Retry-After`, and retry temporary errors with increasing delays. A 503 now stays in the pending state instead of immediately failing, and existing failed tracks with a saved 503 will be retried after you deploy and reopen Puffin.

Changed [metadata-normalization.js](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/web/src/metadata-normalization.js) and [enrichment.js](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/web/src/enrichment.js). All 28 frontend tests and the production build passed.

This can make Puffin recover when MusicBrainz becomes available again; it can’t make MusicBrainz return successfully while the service itself is unavailable.

## Assistant

“Groq ranking unavailable” means a different step failed: Puffin found MusicBrainz candidates, then its `/api/smart-fill/rank` request returned an error. The backend reports a missing `GROQ_API_KEY` as 503; Groq request failures, timeouts, or invalid AI responses are reported as 502. The old saved message doesn’t include the status or response details, so it can’t tell us which one happened.

In the **latest** attempt, MusicBrainz returned 503, so enrichment stopped before Groq ranking. That’s a separate failure, and Groq wasn’t reached on that attempt.

The ranking route is configured in [vercel.json](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/vercel.json) and implemented in [main.py](/Users/admin/Desktop/Puffin/groq-service/main.py). After the newer frontend is deployed, a fresh ranking failure should include the HTTP status and response details in its saved error. Vercel’s function logs for the `smart_fill` service should also show the underlying Groq exception.
